title: Index of international dry bulk freight (Baltic Dry Index, 1985 = 1 000) 2011-2025 by month
publisher: Statistics and Research Aland (ASUB), official statistics of Aland
licence: ASUB open statistics (free use with attribution); the table cites Capital Link as its source and the index itself is produced by the Baltic Exchange
limitations: A monthly figure for a daily index; the table documentation defines the monthly value (see metadata notes).
Secondary publication of Baltic Exchange data compiled by Capital Link; the Baltic Exchange is the originator of the index.
The table is updated by ASUB after each year end, so the latest month lags the demand data.

variables: json-stat source field: Capital Link (https://capitallinkshipping.com/); dataset updated field: 2016-01-26T22:00:00Z

title: Brazil Comex Stat: monthly exports by destination country for iron ore, soybeans, maize, soybean meal, sugar, manganese ore, bauxite and wood chips
publisher: Ministerio do Desenvolvimento, Industria, Comercio e Servicos (MDIC), Brazil
licence: Open government data (Brazilian open data policy); attribution to MDIC/Comex Stat
limitations: Destination is the declared country of destination at export, which can differ from the final discharge port.
Figures for the latest two months are preliminary and revised in later releases; the last two years are refreshed every run.

title: IMF PortWatch: daily port activity and chokepoint transits (AIS-based)
publisher: International Monetary Fund and University of Oxford (PortWatch)
licence: Free for non-commercial and research use under the IMF PortWatch terms of use; attribution required
frequency: daily (aggregated here to months and to global daily totals)
units: metric tons of cargo (import and export estimates), number of port calls, number of transits
limitations: Volumes are statistical estimates derived from AIS draught changes and vessel capacity, not customs data.
Export and import tonnage are estimated independently, so world exports and world imports differ.
The ports database covers roughly 2,000 ports; small terminals are not covered.
Chokepoint capacity is deadweight capacity of transiting vessels, not cargo on board.
Known reporting gaps (blackout days) and GPS interference episodes are documented on the PortWatch site.

title: World Port Index (Pub. 150), port locations and characteristics
publisher: US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA), Maritime Safety Information
limitations: A port coordinate is a single reference point; large export terminals can lie several miles from it.

title: OECD Composite Leading Indicators, amplitude adjusted (long-term average = 100)
publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
licence: OECD terms and conditions (free reuse with attribution, CC BY 4.0 for OECD data)
limitations: Recent months are revised as the cycle is re-estimated; each refresh stores the current vintage.
A leading indicator of the general business cycle, not of dry bulk trade specifically.

title: UN Comtrade: monthly bilateral trade in iron ore, coal and lignite, grains and soybeans (net weight)
licence: UN Comtrade public data; free for non-commercial use with attribution (see Comtrade terms of use)
frequency: monthly from 2010; annual from 2000 (long history and annual unit values)
coverage: 2010-01 to latest published month per reporter; 4 reporter groups
units: kilograms (netWgt); values in current US dollars (primaryValue)
limitations: Reporter customs data are used as reported; mirror flows between two reporters differ by timing, valuation and routing.
Monthly data are revised by reporters; the last 15 months are refreshed on every run.
Mode of transport is not separated for most reporters, so overland flows between neighbours are excluded by route design.
China publishes monthly detail to Comtrade with a lag of more than a year, so China-reported series are used only for cross-checks, not for the monthly panel.
The public preview API returns at most 500 records per call and enforces hourly call quotas; queries are split so that no response is truncated and the client waits when the quota is exhausted.

groups.note: India reports imports; Russia and Mozambique do not report timely data; Japan reports imports of Russian coal; mirror check only

title: UNCTADstat maritime transport statistics: merchant fleet, ships built and scrapped, port calls, seaborne trade
publisher: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), UNCTADstat Data Centre
licence: UNCTADstat data may be freely used with attribution to UNCTAD (UNCTADstat terms of use)
coverage: US.MerchantFleet: 1980 to 2026; US.ShipBuilding: 2014 to 2025; US.ShipScrapping: 2014 to 2025; US.PortCalls: 2018 to 2023; US.SeaborneTrade: 2000 to 2024; US.PortCalls_S: 2018S01 to 2023S02; US.PortCallsArrivals: 2018 to 2023
units: thousand deadweight tons (fleet, 1 January), gross tons (ships built and scrapped), days (median time in port), thousand metric tons (seaborne trade)
limitations: Fleet figures are stocks as of 1 January, compiled from Clarksons Research data for ships of 100 GT and above.
Ships built and scrapped are not split by ship type in the public dataset; they describe the whole fleet.
Median time in port is an annual median across all port calls in the ship type and may hide within-year swings.
Seaborne trade dry cargo includes containerised and minor bulk cargo, not only the major bulks.

title: World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook, monthly prices (Pink Sheet)
licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), as stated by the World Bank for its datasets
units: US dollars per metric ton (iron ore: per dry metric ton unit; Brent: per barrel; gas: per mmbtu)
limitations: Prices are benchmark assessments, not transaction volumes.
Brent crude is a proxy for marine bunker fuel prices, which are not published free of charge.
Series definitions change occasionally (for example the coal benchmark basis); the workbook footnotes apply.
